user.title: Set up TrueTemp
user.description: TrueTemp works out what outdoor temperature to show your heat pump so the house actually lands on the temperature you asked for. It learns your house by itself — there is nothing to tune.

data.name: Name
data.heating_type: How the heat gets into the room

data_description.indoor_temp_sensor: Pick a sensor in a room you actually live in, away from direct sun and draughts. This becomes the zone's primary sensor — its identity, and, if you add extra sensors below, the one member of the average that never drops out. Everything is learned from the combined reading, so a cupboard or a basement will teach it the wrong house.
data_description.indoor_temp_sensors_extra: Optional, up to four more. Combined with the sensor above using the mode below — useful for a house where one room runs colder than the rest, or to stop a single sensor's glitches from being read as a real temperature change.
data_description.indoor_aggregation: Average takes the mean of every reporting sensor. Lowest heats to the coldest room — the house settles with every other room above target, and the price-saving floor then protects that coldest room instead of the average one. Only matters once you've added extra sensors above.
data_description.outdoor_temp_sensor: A real outdoor sensor if you have one — it is usually more accurate than a weather service estimate.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Used for the sun and wind forecast. You can add or change this later.
data_description.nordpool_price_entity: Optional. A Nordpool sensor with today's and tomorrow's hourly prices, needed to save money on electricity. You can add or change this later.
data_description.indoor_target_temperature: You can change this any time from the thermostat, by voice, or on a schedule.
data_description.heating_type: Only used for the first few days. After that, TrueTemp has measured how quickly your house responds and stops relying on this answer.

data_description.enable_data_logging: Writes one line per cycle to a file in your config folder. Nothing leaves your machine. Useful if you ever want to check how well it has been doing.

sources.title: Sun, wind and price sensors
sources.description: Optional extras. Sun and wind let TrueTemp react before the house has started to drift; a price sensor lets it save money when electricity is expensive.

data_description.weather_entity: Only used for the sun and wind forecast. Not needed if both are switched off below.
data_description.nordpool_price_entity: A Nordpool sensor with today's and tomorrow's hourly prices. Without one, price saving does nothing.
data_description.enable_solar_input: Backs off a little when the sun is warming the house. Only switch this on if your indoor sensor — or, with more than one configured, their combined reading — is somewhere the sun actually reaches. A sensor in a basement, a north-facing room or a hallway never sees the solar gain, so this would push the temperature down for a warming nothing you measure can confirm.
data_description.enable_wind_input: Adds a little when wind is stripping heat out of the house. Leave this off unless you have an older, draughty house that you can feel getting colder in high wind. A reasonably sealed house barely responds to wind, and compensating for an effect that is not there just adds noise.
data_description.enable_weather_lookahead: Starts heating a little harder before a cold front or a rising wind actually arrives, instead of waiting for the house to cool first. Sun works the other way: it holds heat back before a burst of sunshine arrives, so the house doesn't overheat once the sun's own warmth lands. Each fades out as its change lands. Needs the weather forecast entity above.

price.title: Saving money on electricity
price.description: When electricity is expensive, TrueTemp can let the house drift slightly cooler and make it up when prices fall. How far it will drift is set on the zone's Price saving control; how careful it is when it is properly cold is set on Cold caution.

data.enable_price_compensation: Save money when electricity is expensive
data.comfort_min_c: Never let it get colder than

data_description.enable_price_compensation: Needs an electricity price sensor on the previous page.
data_description.comfort_min_c: A hard floor. No amount of saving will take the house below this.
data_description.price_significance_floor: Below this much difference between today's cheapest and most expensive hour, braking and pre-charging fade out rather than react — protects a persistently cheap stretch from chasing swings too small to be worth the comfort trade. Leave at 0 for automatic (scaled to your typical local price level); enter a number in your price sensor's own unit to fix it yourself.

output.title: Outgoing sensors
output.description: By default TrueTemp only publishes a sensor and you wire that to your heat pump yourself. These options let it send the value out for you instead. Pick an output method below and the next page will ask for what it needs.

output_spoof.title: Spoofing the outdoor sensor
output_spoof.description: The two ways of doing this can be combined, used alone, or left both empty.

output_number_push.name: Send to a number entity
output_number_push.description: For example number.ohmigo_temperature, if you already have your OhmOnWifi or Ohmigo device set up in Home Assistant.

ohmonwifi_direct.name: Send straight to an OhmOnWifi device
ohmonwifi_direct.description: Talks to the device over your local network with no Home Assistant entity in between. Enter its name (usually ohmonwifiplus.local) or its IP address. This is checked when you save.

output_curve.title: The heat pump's own offset
output_curve.description: For pumps that let you set "heat curve or outdoor temp offset" directly, instead of faking the outdoor sensor.

data.heat_curve_offset_invert: This pump's offset works the other way round

data_description.heat_curve_offset_invert: Leave off if a higher number on your pump means more heat, which is the case for most pumps. Switch on if it is the other way round for yours.

output_indoor_climate.title: Steering an indoor climate entity
output_indoor_climate.description: For pumps or thermostatic radiator valves that expose their own room-sensor climate entity, instead of faking the outdoor sensor or a curve offset.

vacation.title: Vacation plans
vacation.description: Add, edit, remove or reorder plans. Only enabled plans whose windows don't overlap can be saved.

vacation_add.title: Add a vacation plan
vacation_add.description: Set the plan's name, whether it's enabled, how it repeats, and the lowest temperature allowed while you're away.

vacation_edit_fields.title: Edit vacation plan
vacation_edit_fields.description: Change the plan's name, whether it's enabled, how it repeats, and the lowest temperature allowed while you're away.

vacation_once.title: Dates
vacation_once.description: The plan is active from the start date to the end date.

vacation_weekly.title: Weekly window
vacation_weekly.description: The plan repeats every week between these days and times.

vacation_yearly.title: Yearly window
vacation_yearly.description: The plan repeats every year between these dates.

vacation_reorder.title: Reorder vacation plans
vacation_reorder.description: When more than one enabled plan is active at the same time, the one higher in the list wins.

outdoor_sensor_unavailable.title: TrueTemp ({name}) has lost its outdoor sensor
outdoor_sensor_unavailable.description: {entity_id} is unavailable or not reporting a number, so TrueTemp cannot publish a compensated value. It will keep retrying and this warning clears itself once the sensor is readable again.

indoor_sensor_unavailable.title: TrueTemp ({name}) has lost its indoor reading
indoor_sensor_unavailable.description: None of the {total} configured indoor sensors are reporting a number ({entity_id}). TrueTemp is holding the learned offset and pausing learning until at least one comes back — nothing else is affected.

indoor_sensor_partial.title: TrueTemp ({name}) is missing some indoor sensors
indoor_sensor_partial.description: Only {count} of {total} configured indoor sensors are reporting — {entity_id} is not. TrueTemp is still controlling normally on the sensors it has; this clears itself once they come back.

indoor_sensor_missing.title: TrueTemp ({name}) can't find a configured indoor sensor
indoor_sensor_missing.description: {entity_id} no longer exists in Home Assistant — it was renamed or its integration was removed. TrueTemp keeps running on any other configured sensors, but this needs to be fixed in the zone's settings; it will not clear itself.

wind_forecast_unavailable.title: TrueTemp ({name}) has lost its wind forecast
wind_forecast_unavailable.description: The weather entity {entity_id} has no wind reading right now, so wind compensation is contributing nothing this cycle.

cloud_sun_forecast_unavailable.title: TrueTemp ({name}) has lost its sun/cloud forecast
cloud_sun_forecast_unavailable.description: The weather entity {entity_id} has no cloud reading right now, so sun compensation is contributing nothing this cycle.

price_unavailable.title: TrueTemp ({name}) has lost its electricity price
price_unavailable.description: {entity_id} is unavailable, so price-based saving is contributing nothing this cycle.
